chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 483: The new emperor recognizes Li Huowang!
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang's Office errand goes sideways when he runs into the new Great Liang Emperor—the same boy who once conned him for 500 silver on Shangsi Festival.
og_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 483 — The awkward moment you try to hide from the new emperor
og_description: Li Huowang goofs, almost gets stabbed by the Grand Preceptor, and then the teenage ruler recognizes him from a fake jade cat heist.
twitter_title: Chapter 483: Li Huowang, invisible and sheepish before the teenager he once tried to buy a fake cat from.
twitter_description: Turns out the ruler you don't kneel to is the same kid who sold you a counterfeit for 500 taels. Awkward.

lore_anchors.definition: An ancient Chinese festival celebrated on the third day of the third lunar month, associated with spring outings, cleansing rituals, and—in this novel—meeting romantic interests.
The name of the empire in the Dao-Twisted World; note its rapid imperial turnover (three emperors in months) signals deep political fragility.
The emperor's supreme Daoist advisor and ritual official; in this chapter, an old blind-eyed Daoist who can detect invisible intruders and lock bodies with supernatural force.
Administrative structures on the palace periphery, distinct from the golden inner halls; where official business (like the Office) is conducted rather than court ceremonies.
The Grand Steward of the palace eunuchs; a former Supervisory Heavenly Office member, now a powerful intermediary between the throne and the Office.
The identity token of a Supervisory Heavenly Office operative; its display de-escalates a potentially fatal confrontation with palace guards.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the Grand Preceptor detect Li Huowang's invisibility so easily?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because he is an extremely powerful cultivator who already fought the Zuowandao in a previous battle; his blind-eye-opening trick is a sign of a far higher cultivation level Li Huowang cannot ignore.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the "fake cat" Li Huowang remembers?
cultural_notes_faq.a: During the Shangsi Festival in an earlier chapter, a young boy (now revealed as the crown prince) tricked Li Huowang into buying a painted, fake jade cat for 500 silver taels. The emperor recognizes Li Huowang from that prank.
